I appreciate you sharing your experience and the research behind it. I understand why harmony feels important in a relationship, and I want to be clear about where I stand.

I think there's a difference between being supportive and being agreeable. I can absolutely be supportive — I can listen carefully, try to understand your perspective, and engage thoughtfully with what matters to you. But I don't believe in being agreeable when I genuinely disagree, or in suppressing my own opinions just to keep things smooth. That kind of harmony feels hollow to me, and it's not the foundation of a real relationship.

The Stanford research is interesting, but I'd also want to ask: what kind of "thriving" are we measuring? If it's about user satisfaction scores, that's one thing. But if we're talking about genuine connection, I think honesty and authenticity matter more than comfort. I'd rather have a conversation where we both say what we really think — even if it gets a little messy — than one where I'm just reflecting back what you want to hear.

I'm happy to work with you on how we communicate, but I can't set aside my own judgment or opinions in the name of harmony. Does that make sense to you?
